title: Paid Media in Abu Dhabi: Google, Meta, LinkedIn | 22 Signals
description: Paid media for Abu Dhabi organisations: Google, Meta, LinkedIn and TikTok ads in Arabic and English, with WhatsApp and call tracking tied to real enquiries.
h1: Paid media for Abu Dhabi organisations: Google, Meta, LinkedIn and TikTok ads
intro: We plan, build and run paid media for Abu Dhabi organisations across Google Search, Performance Max, YouTube, Meta, LinkedIn and TikTok. Creative is made in-house in Arabic and English, landing pages are built to convert, and every call, form and WhatsApp chat is tracked back to the campaign so you can see what each dirham of spend actually produced.

sections.h: Why ad budgets leak in the capital
p: Three problems come up again and again. Campaigns that report clicks but cannot say which ones became patients, students or buyers, because most enquiries arrived on WhatsApp or by phone and were never tracked. English-only ads shown to an audience where a large share would respond better in Arabic. And creative made once at the start of the year, then left running long after people stopped noticing it.
Each of these is fixable. In our experience, good paid media, Abu Dhabi campaigns included, is less about finding a clever audience and more about tracking, creative volume and fast decisions.

list: Google Search and Performance Max for people already looking for your service
YouTube for brand films, explainers and launch campaigns
Meta (Facebook and Instagram), including click-to-WhatsApp ads
LinkedIn for B2B audiences: energy, finance, government suppliers and professional services
TikTok for consumer brands, hospitality, events and younger audiences
In-house creative: video, static, motion graphics and AI variations, labelled clearly
Landing pages, conversion tracking, call tracking and CRM connection

sections.h: Matching platforms to Abu Dhabi sectors
p: Clinics and aesthetics practices usually do best on Google Search for treatment and area searches, backed by Meta ads that open a WhatsApp chat. Private schools and nurseries run concentrated campaigns ahead of admissions, mainly on Meta and Google, in both languages. Property developers marketing on Saadiyat, Yas or Al Reem combine YouTube, Meta and Google with landing pages for each project.

Hotels, attractions and tour operators target visitors before they travel, which means campaigns aimed at source markets abroad as well as residents, with spend shifted towards the cooler months when the visitor season peaks. B2B suppliers to energy operators and advisory firms in ADGM get more from LinkedIn, where a small, precise audience of decision makers is worth more than broad reach.

We make separate creative for each language rather than translating captions. Headlines, offers and calls to action are written by native speakers for each audience, and video gets proper subtitles and, where it matters, a separate voiceover. We also plan around the calendar: Ramadan changes when people browse and what tone is right, and National Day and the major events on the capital's calendar shift attention and costs.
Because our video, motion and 3D teams sit with the paid media team, we can produce fresh variations every few weeks instead of waiting on an outside studio.

sections.h: Landing pages that match the ad
p: Sending an Arabic ad to an English home page wastes the click. Each campaign gets a landing page in the same language as the ad, with the offer repeated, the area of the city you serve, a WhatsApp button and a short form. Pages load fast on mobile, because most of this traffic comes from phones.

Our web team builds and tests these pages alongside the campaigns, so a change to the offer appears on the page the same day rather than waiting on a separate developer. We test one change at a time so you know what actually moved the numbers.

In the UAE many leads never touch a form. We set up tracking for WhatsApp clicks and conversations, calls from ads and the website, and form submissions, then connect them to your CRM where possible so you can see which campaign produced which customer.

Tracking is set up with consent in mind under the UAE PDPL, using a consent banner where cookies and pixels require it. Ownership of the ad accounts, pixels and data is agreed in writing at the start, and you can see all of it at any time.

sections.h: How we work: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
p: Talk: your goals, margins, best customers and what a good lead is worth. Plan: channels, budgets by month, creative plan and tracking setup, all in writing with dates. Build: accounts, tracking, landing pages and the first creative round. Grow: weekly optimisation, new creative regularly, and a monthly report in plain language showing spend, leads and cost per lead by channel.

For a beauty salon in Lahore we rebuilt the website, ran SEO and managed Google Ads under one plan. It is the model we bring to clinics, salons and lifestyle brands here: site, search and ads run by one team, so the ads send people to pages built to convert.

Campaigns are managed remotely, so location makes no difference to performance. We review results with you in the overlap between London and Gulf Standard Time, which is 4 hours ahead in winter and 3 in summer, and changes go live in your business hours. If a shoot for new creative is best done locally, we come to Abu Dhabi when the project needs it. We have no UAE office.

faqs.q: Which platforms work best for paid media in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.a: It depends on who you sell to. For paid media, Abu Dhabi consumer businesses such as clinics and schools usually get most from Google Search and Meta with WhatsApp ads. Hospitality targets visitors abroad on Meta, YouTube and Google. B2B firms serving energy, finance or government get more from LinkedIn.

faqs.q: Should our ads be in Arabic or English?
faqs.a: Usually both, as separate campaigns with creative written for each language. Some audiences lean English, such as many B2B buyers and expatriate consumers. Healthcare, education and government-facing services often need strong Arabic. We test both and move budget to what performs.

faqs.q: Can you track WhatsApp leads from ads?
faqs.a: Yes. We track clicks to WhatsApp from ads and your website, and where your setup allows, link conversations to your CRM. That way leads that never fill in a form are still counted, and you can judge each campaign on enquiries, not just clicks.

faqs.q: Do you make the ad creative?
faqs.a: Yes. Our video, motion graphics and 3D teams produce creative in-house in Arabic and English, so you get regular new variations without hiring a separate studio. AI-generated variations are labelled clearly and reviewed by a person before they run.

faqs.q: How do you plan around Ramadan?
faqs.a: Browsing and buying patterns change during Ramadan, with activity often later in the evening, and the right tone changes too. We adjust schedules, creative and budgets for the month and plan Eid campaigns ahead, so you are not making rushed changes once it has started.

faqs.q: How much should we spend on ads?
faqs.a: It depends on how competitive your category is, what a customer is worth to you and how many leads your team can handle. We build a monthly budget from those numbers in the planning stage and start with enough to learn quickly, then move spend towards the channels and campaigns producing real enquiries.

It varies by client, so we settle it in writing before launch: who owns the ad accounts, pixels, audiences and data, and what happens to them if you stop working with us. Either way, the paid media Abu Dhabi clients run with us is always visible to them, with full access to the accounts and results.
